template.title: CAREER: HIGH-RESOLUTION NMR FOR PARAMAGNETIC SODIUM

question.text: Battery material samples will be synthesized in powder form and identified through a consistent and

json.answer: systematic labeling procedure, which will include sample composition, name of researcher and date.

question.text: Experimental data generated over the course of the research will include synthesis procedures and

json.answer:
results from characterization of battery electrode samples. Digital characterization data in tabular
form will be produced by electrochemical testing, X-ray diffraction, solid-state NMR spectroscopy,

question.text: EPR spectroscopy, magnetometry, impedance spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron and absorption

json.answer: spectroscopy, and Mössbauer spectroscopy measurements. Rietveld refinements of scattering data

question.text: will generate crystallographic data. Scanning electron microscopy will generate images. Synthetic

json.answer:
work and optimization of NMR experimental procedures will be documented in lab notebooks and
generate physical data. The Van der Ven group’s CASM software will be extended to enable the

question.text: simulation of finite temperature NMR spectra of paramagnetic materials. First principles and Monte

json.answer: Carlo simulations will produce text files, density of states plots and two-dimensional charge density

question.text: maps. Educational and outreach materials, and assessment results, will be digitized.

section.title: Data Format Standards
section.description: In order to allow for interoperability, reproducibility, and reuse, all data will be stored and saved in

question.text: Data Format Standards

json.answer: standard and open formats. Experimental characterization data will be stored and saved as, e.g.,

question.text: ASCII, CSV, Word, Matlab and Python files. Microscope images will be stored as portable graphic

json.answer:
files (.tif, .jpg or .png format). Crystallographic data will be reported in standard crystallographic
information framework (*.cif) format to facilitate visualization and further analysis through widely
available software tools (VESTA, cif2file, etc.). Crystallographic data for previously-unreported

question.text: compounds/structures will be uploaded to the ICSD database. First principles simulation input and

json.answer:
output files (generated with the VASP and CRYSTAL codes) will be stored as rich text format (*.rtf)
files for readability across many programs and platforms. The CRYSTAL code manual will be
provided along CRYSTAL input/output data to allow for interpretation of variables. Both

question.text: CRYSTAL and VASP manuals are also available online. The Van der Ven group's CASM software

json.answer:
currently interfaces with VASP, automates the construction of effective Hamiltonians and subjects
them to Monte Carlo simulations. CASM organizes all the files associated with VASP calculations
into a standard structure that can be accessed by subsequent runs of CASM, either by the same user

question.text: or by a new user. A similar CASM interface and infrastructure will be developed here for

json.answer:
CRYSTAL calculations of NMR properties. The uniform file structure enforced by CASM for the
effective Hamiltonian construction and the large number of Monte Carlo simulations that are

question.text: necessary to construct, e.g., temperature composition phase diagrams, will be extended to include

json.answer:
Fermi contact shifts and electric field gradient tensors. This will ensure that results from calculations
performed by different users are in a format that is readily accessible, either by CASM or directly by
different people.

question.text: The Program Toolkit and Activity Plans developed for the educational and outreach activities in

json.answer: partnership with Jamboree Housing (JH) will be uploaded to JH’s filesharing system for broad and

question.text: free dissemination to their different centers and partners in California. All of the research results will

json.answer:
be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, and annual reports.
The supporting information accompanying publications will include detailed
experimental/simulation/synthetic procedures, as well as detailed information on models used for

question.text: data analysis. All of the journals of interest to the group make supporting information files publicly-

json.answer:
available online free of charge. In addition, all publication pre-prints will be made freely available,
along with supplementary information, on the UC eScholarship website.

question.text: Over the course of the project, digital data will be internally stored and shared for collaborative work

json.answer:
on the UCSB-administered, Box platform with unlimited cloud storage. The privacy, security and
intellectual property protection of data stored in this manner are guaranteed by the privacy policy
and terms of service contract between University of California and Box. As a means of making data

question.text: accessible and searchable, data collected over the course of this project will be stored in the data

json.answer:
repository Dryad. enables easy data upload and description, and creates digital object
identifiers (DOIs) for each dataset to help manage long-term data sharing through digital
organization. We note that CASM systematically organizes all first-principles calculations that have

question.text: been performed on a given system and has tools to query a wide range of properties for each

json.answer:
calculation. Furthermore, any structure with a chemical ordering, magnetic ordering or a structural
distortion that has been made "by hand" can be imported in a CASM project and made to be
consistent with the automatically enumerated configurations. Hence, for each system of interest to

question.text: this work, a structured CASM results packet that can easily be queried will be created (consisting of

json.answer:
the results of electronic structure calculations, effective Hamiltonian interaction parameters and basis
functions and Monte Carlo results) and uploaded to Dryad. is free of charge for UCSB
researchers and can be accessed using a personal ORCID.

question.text: CASM is an open source software package released under the GNU Lesser General Public License

json.answer:
(LGPL) and available free of charge via the prisms-center conda channel at
https://anaconda.org/prisms-center. All additions of the CASM software developed during this
project will be incorporated into the CASM software and made accessible free of charge and open

question.text: source under a similar LGPL license. Demonstrations on how to access and use CASM’s NMR

json.answer:
extensions (and conditions under which they can use and modify the code) will be uploaded to the
CASM software website: https://prisms-center.github.io/CASMcode_docs/.

section.title: Policies and provisions for re-use, re-distribution, and production of derivatives
section.description: All data will be stored in Dryad and will be available under a public domain, creative commons

question.text: Policies and provisions for re-use, re-distribution, and production of derivatives

json.answer: license (CC0). Note that while a personal ORCID is needed to deposit data in Dryad, no ORCID is

question.text: required to search, find and download datasets.

json.answer:
The existing open source software infrastructure within CASM that serves as a foundation to this
project, is already licensed by the Regents of the University of California under the ``LGPL'' open
source license, and distributed via the prisms-center conda channel, permitting non-exclusive use of

question.text: the software. Additions to CASM will be released as LGPL to follow the current licensing of

json.answer: CASM.

section.title: Archiving of Data, Samples, and Other Relevant Research Products
section.description: Laboratory notebooks and samples will be retained for a minimum of 5 years following the

question.text: Archiving of Data, Samples, and Other Relevant Research Products

json.answer: conclusion of the program and will remain the property of UC Santa Barbara and kept on campus

question.text: after students graduate. All digital data produced over the course of the project and stored on Box

json.answer: will be moved to Dryad after completion of the project for indefinite storage (>5 years).
